messages:
maria: quick report - ran into a nasty edge case in the kotlin sample app when sending large gzipped uploads from emulator (Pixel 7a API 33/34). observed duplicate POSTs where server processed the same upload twice with different auth tokens. minimal repro below. anyone seen this pattern before?

maria: high level: app streams gzip RequestBody to avoid OOM, server returns 401 mid-way (expired token), our Authenticator does a synchronous refresh and returns a follow-up request. sometimes okhttp also triggers a connection-recovery retry (EPIPE) during the write which ends up sending the payload twice.

maria: server log snippet: 
```
[upload-svc] 2026-03-02T09:12:10.010Z POST /v1/upload 401 "Auth: Bearer tok_old"
[upload-svc] 2026-03-02T09:12:10.140Z POST /v1/upload 200 "Auth: Bearer tok_new"
```

maria: sample RequestBody used in toy app: 
```kotlin
val streamingBody = object : RequestBody() {
  override fun contentType() = "application/gzip".toMediaType()
  override fun writeTo(sink: BufferedSink) {
    GzipSink(sink).use { gz -> inputStream.source().use { it.readAll(gz) } }
  }
}
```

kai: interesting. OkHttp typically won't replay a streaming body unless it can safely recover. If the socket fails early (EPIPE) during the write, OkHttp's internal recover path may try to retry the call. Separately, Authenticator returning a follow-up request after 401 can reproduce the call. If both trigger, you get two attempts. Check client config: is retryOnConnectionFailure enabled?

maria: client is default (retryOnConnectionFailure=true). no manual replay or special interceptors.

omar: likely concurrency of two mechanisms. If the server closes connection mid-write causing EPIPE, OkHttp tries to recover; if the server later responds 401, the Authenticator will also issue a new request. Because streaming bodies are not rewindable, this is a dangerous overlap. Repro on emulator suggests the write fails then the 401 path races.

lina: I instrumented the sampleapp and reproduced reliably on emulator image. captured thread dump and logs: 
```
OkHttp: write() -> IOException: EPIPE
AuthenticatorBridge: runBlocking refresh -> got new token
OkHttp: attemptRecoverForWrite -> retry scheduled (uses connection-retry path)
```

lina: disabling retryOnConnectionFailure in the client removed the duplicate POST in my runs. But that's not ideal for general reliability.

kai: recommendations: 1) avoid running long blocking refresh in Authenticator (it's synchronous). If you call suspending refresh via runBlocking on OkHttp's thread pool you can stall IO threads. Prefer doing token refresh outside the Authenticator in a suspend-capable interceptor or ensure single-flight refresh (mutex) so only one refresh happens. 2) For large streaming uploads, provide a small buffered prefix (eg 8KB) that is rewindable so short retries can be handled without buffering entire file. 3) if streaming is necessary, consider setting retryOnConnectionFailure=false for that call.

maria: thinking of two practical changes for the sampleapp: (A) update sample client to set retryOnConnectionFailure=false for upload client and document why, (B) change the sample Authenticator to use a single-flight refresh guarded by a mutex and avoid runBlocking on IO threads. I'll open a PR with both.

omar: also add an automated emulator test to our CI matrix that reproduces EPIPE + 401 on API 33/34. CI flaky currently missed this until we created the deterministic tiny server that closes connection mid-write.

kai: small code snippet to share with sample app authors: 
```kotlin
// simple single-flight refresh example
private val refreshLock = Mutex()
suspend fun getFreshToken(): String = refreshLock.withLock {
  if (tokenValid()) return currentToken
  val new = doNetworkRefresh() // suspend call
  currentToken = new
  return new
}
// hook this into an interceptor that can suspend; avoid doing runBlocking in Authenticator
```

lina: I'll add a short doc note in devex explaining streaming + auth interactions and the retryOnConnectionFailure caveat. also add the prefix-buffer trick example (first 8kb).

ci-bot: CI: reproducible-upload-race branch failed on emulator-14 matrix - test UploadRetryRaceTest failed consistently (see PR #1219 for logs).

maria: thanks everyone. I'll push the PR with: disable retryOnConnectionFailure for upload client, mutex-based refresh example, and a small note in DX docs about tradeoffs. tagging @kai @lina for quick sign-off. :sparkles:
